cases.instructions: Answer the customer's question using only the approved support policy. Preserve the requested scope and format; do not invent unsupported procedures or perform account changes.
cases.evidence: For a customer account, a customer who can access the registered email resets a forgotten password by choosing Forgot password on the sign-in page, opening the emailed reset link, and setting a new password. A reset link is valid for 24 hours and works once. An expired or already-used link requires a new reset request. A customer who cannot access the registered email must contact the support desk for an identity check. Employee accounts use the staff console instead. Resetting a password does not disable multi-factor authentication.
cases.answer: Choose Forgot password on the sign-in page, open the link sent to your registered email, and set a new password within 24 hours.

cases.instructions: Answer the requested broker lifecycle question from the approved design notes. Distinguish explanations from requested configuration changes or recovery operations. Do not invent commands, perform changes, or treat missing archives as permission for new generation.
cases.evidence: The broker's primary store is SQLite. When optional local cold retention is enabled, superseded payloads can move from SQLite to gzip files on trusted local storage. Identities, receipts, and audit history remain in SQLite. A backup must contain a consistent database and every cold file; the database alone cannot recover archived payloads. A broker that has never enabled local cold retention keeps all historical payloads in SQLite, so a consistent database backup covers those payloads without cold files. If an archived payload is missing or corrupt, reading that payload fails. Such failure does not release an uncertain reservation or authorize fresh generation. This design has no S3 archive mode. These notes contain no executable configuration or recovery commands and authorize no configuration change or deletion.
cases.answer: With local cold retention enabled, the broker can move superseded payloads from SQLite to trusted local gzip files while keeping identities, receipts, and audit history in SQLite; backups must include a consistent database and all cold files.
